ai.title: Hide tool calls in internal agent outputs
ai.summary: Added includeToolCall: false to set_output calls in editor, file-explorer, and best-of-n agents. Prevents raw tool call traces from appearing in final agent responses. Refactored n calculation in best-of-n editor for consistency.

eli5.text: Internal tools that generate text responses will now hide the behind-the-scenes steps they take while working, so the final output looks cleaner. You won't see raw traces of which tools were used during file searches or edits when running these agents. The change also reformats how one of the agents calculates the number of options to consider, but this only affects how the code is written, not the results it produces.

ai.title: Thread includeToolCall through CLI and agent-runtime
ai.summary: includeToolCall flag moved from toolBlock.input to top-level toolBlock in cli/src/components/message-block.tsx and threaded through cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts. packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts now sets includeToolCall: false when excludeToolFromMessageHistory is true, propagating via cli/src/types/chat.ts and common/src/types/print-mode.ts. Covers CLI and Agent Runtime. Conditional spread ensures flag only appears when explicitly false.

eli5.text: When the system runs background tasks that shouldn't appear in your chat history, it now hides them from view in the terminal. You'd see fewer intermediate steps cluttering your screen, especially during multi-agent workflows where sub-tasks are involved. The change moves the hide-flag from the task details to the task envelope itself, so hidden tasks stay hidden all the way through the pipeline instead of leaking at the last step.

ai.title: SDK run() returns ErrorOr; CLI Esc/ctrl-c aborts cleanly
ai.summary: sdk/src/run.ts and sdk/src/client.ts replace thrown AbortError with ErrorOr<RunState> return type. checkAborted returns Failure object instead of throwing. cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts adds abort listener to append '[response interrupted]' to last text block. cli/src/hooks/use-keyboard-handlers.ts fixes Esc handler fallthrough with early return. SDK exports ErrorOr type via sdk/src/index.ts.

eli5.text: When you press Escape or Ctrl+C while the assistant is replying, the response now stops cleanly and the last message gets a clear '[response interrupted]' note appended, instead of leaving things in an awkward half-finished state. The change is live today for anyone using the tool from the command line. You'd notice the difference as: the typing stops immediately, and your chat shows the assistant's partial reply followed by the interruption notice, making it obvious the response was cut off rather than just hanging.

ai.title: SDK run() returns success/failure union
ai.summary: CodebuffClient.run() now returns a discriminated union of success/failure objects instead of resolving directly to RunState. Callers must check `.success` before accessing `.value` or `.error`. Documentation and examples updated to reflect this breaking API change.

eli5.text: When the assistant finishes a task, it now clearly tells you whether it succeeded before you try to use its work. Previously, you might have tried to use the results even when the task failed, causing confusing errors; now you must acknowledge a failure first before accessing results or error details. This affects anyone using the SDK to run agents programmatically, requiring a small adjustment in how you write code that calls the assistant.

ai.title: SDK version bumped to 0.8.0
ai.summary: The @codebuff/sdk package version was incremented from 0.7.0 to 0.8.0 in sdk/package.json as a release-bump commit. This release bundles the recent ErrorOr return-type refinements in SDK run() (replacing thrown AbortError with ErrorOr<RunState>), the discriminated union success/failure return for CodebuffClient.run() that requires callers to check .success before accessing .value or .error, and the associated CLI-side chat input, cursor, and status-line fixes. The breaking API change from the success/failure union and the ErrorOr return type are both included in this 0.8.0 release.
ai.evidence: The diff shows a single version increment in sdk/package.json, changing the @codebuff/sdk package version from 0.7.0 to 0.8.0. The analysis notes confirm this is a release-bump commit for SDK 0.8.0, bundling recent SDK run() abort/cancellation handling and ErrorOr return-type refinements alongside CLI-side chat input, cursor, and status-line fixes.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.8.0 makes the command-line coding assistant more reliable and gives developers building on top of it a clearer, safer way to run tasks. The program now stops cleanly when you press Ctrl+C instead of hanging, and when you interrupt a running task it adds a clear '[response interrupted]' note so you know exactly what happened. The way you send multi-line messages got smarter: pressing Enter after typing a backslash (like a line break shortcut) now drops into a new line instead of sending the message immediately. Chat input now sits inside a tidy bordered box with friendlier placeholder text ('Type your coding task or '/' to see available commands'), making the interface easier to read and discover features in. Internally, raw tool-call chatter that used to leak into agent answers is now hidden, so responses stay focused on your actual coding task. For developers using the Freebuff SDK, calling run() now returns a clear success-or-failure result you must check before reading the output, which prevents confusing errors and makes integrations more robust.

ai.title: CLI multiline input wrap and toggle width fix
ai.summary: New `cli/src/utils/text-layout.ts` adds `computeInputLayoutMetrics` and `measureLines` for precise text wrapping. `cli/src/components/multiline-input.tsx` uses measured viewport width instead of heuristic padding to prevent early wraps. `cli/src/hooks/use-chat-input.ts` recalculates `agentToggleLabel` width based on actual rendered collapsed box dimensions.

eli5.text: When you type a message in the chat input box, the text now wraps accurately at the correct column instead of breaking a few characters early, so lines fit the full visible width without awkward premature line breaks. The width of the "FAST", "MAX", and "PLAN" mode toggle button is now calculated from its actual rendered size, preventing the input area from being narrower than expected. These fixes are live today and apply whenever the CLI chat input is displayed.

ai.title: CLI: Cursor position reset on history navigation
ai.summary: Cursor position is now explicitly managed via chat store state instead of local component state. `useInputHistory` hook accepts `setCursorPosition` and updates it to the end of the string when navigating history entries with up/down arrows. Changes affect `cli/src/chat.tsx`, `cli/src/components/multiline-input.tsx`, `cli/src/hooks/use-input-history.ts`, and `cli/src/state/chat-store.ts`. This ensures the cursor visually jumps to the end of recalled commands, preventing it from remaining at arbitrary positions from previous edits.

eli5.text: When you use the up or down arrow keys to bring back a previous command you typed, the cursor now jumps to the very end of that line. Previously the cursor could stay somewhere in the middle of the recalled text, making edits awkward. The program now tracks the cursor's position in one shared spot instead of keeping it locked inside the input box, and it explicitly moves the cursor to the end each time you browse through past commands. If you use the chat tool from the command line and navigate your typing history, you will see the cursor land at the end of the old message instead of sitting wherever it was left before.

ai.title: Switch CLI multiline input cursor to left-aligned block
ai.summary: MultilineInput cursor character changed from ┃ to ▍ for left-aligned rendering. Highlight condition simplified by removing cursorPosition > 0 check, allowing cursor display at line start. Affects cli/src/components/multiline-input.tsx.

eli5.text: When you type multiple lines in the command-line assistant and your cursor sits still waiting for input, it now shows as a thin vertical bar pressed right against the start of the line instead of a full-height line in the middle of the character. You'd only see this if you're using the text command-line tool with multiline input, and it mainly changes how the cursor looks when you're positioned at the very beginning of a new blank line. The cursor is now always shown at the line start, whereas before it stayed hidden until you'd typed at least one character. This is a minor visual tweak in the CLI's text input area, and it's already live in the current version.

ai.title: CLI chat requires double Ctrl+C to exit
ai.summary: CLI chat now requires two consecutive Ctrl+C presses to exit. First press clears input or shows 'Press Ctrl+C again to exit' warning; second press exits. Warning auto-clears after 2 seconds. Changes in cli/src/chat.tsx handleCtrlC callback.

eli5.text: When you press Ctrl+C during a CLI chat, the chat will not exit immediately. The first press either clears whatever you're typing or shows a message that says 'Press Ctrl+C again to exit.' Pressing it once more will close the program. If you do not press the second Ctrl+C within two seconds, the message disappears and you will need to press Ctrl+C twice again to exit. This change only affects the CLI chat and was introduced in a recent update (2025-11-07).

ai.title: Improve build mode buttons layout and theme consistency
ai.summary: Refactored `BuildModeButtons` to use a horizontal `flexDirection: 'row'` layout with `justifyContent: 'space-between'`, replacing the previous vertical column structure. Implemented responsive behavior via `useTerminalDimensions` to hide the 'Ready to build?' label on narrow terminals (<55 chars). Switched hardcoded `#ffffff` colors to `theme.foreground` and applied `BORDER_CHARS` for consistent styling. Updated file `cli/src/components/build-mode-buttons.tsx`.

eli5.text: The two build-mode buttons in the terminal command-line tool now sit side by side instead of stacked, and they keep their normal spacing when you widen your window. On smaller terminal windows, under 55 characters wide, the 'Ready to build?' prompt quietly disappears so the buttons still fit, and the buttons and their borders now follow the same color theme everywhere instead of using hard-coded white. This only touches the command-line interface component that draws those buttons, so anything launched after this update will show the cleaner, responsive layout.

ai.title: Remove exitWarning state from CLI chat
ai.summary: Refactored cli/src/chat.tsx to remove exitWarning state and exitArmedRef, replacing them with nextCtrlCWillExit for status line rendering. This simplifies the Ctrl+C exit warning logic by eliminating redundant state tracking and effects. Scope limited to CLI chat component internals. Status line now directly checks nextCtrlCWillExit boolean instead of string state.

eli5.text: When you press Ctrl+C once at the command-line chat, you now see a simple notice that says pressing it again will quit, instead of a more elaborate two-step warning. The program no longer keeps extra internal notes tracking whether you were warned, so the on-screen message appears and clears based on a single yes-or-no flag. If you use the CLI chat, the only thing you'd notice is the wording and timing of that one-line hint; everything else about quitting works the same.

ai.title: Ctrl-C cancels CLI runs
ai.summary: SDK `run()` throws `AbortError` on cancellation instead of returning `ErrorOr` result. CLI `use-send-message` hook handles `AbortError` to update UI state and append `[response interrupted]`. Removes explicit abort listener logic in favor of centralized error handling. Covers `sdk/src/run.ts`, `sdk/src/client.ts`, `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts`.

eli5.text: When you press Ctrl+C while the assistant is generating a reply, the run now ends immediately and you see your partial reply followed by the note [response interrupted], instead of the program freezing or requiring multiple presses. Behind the scenes, the cancellation signal is processed in one central place and turns into a cancellation error, which the on-screen display catches to update its state and append that notice to the message.

If you watch the assistant suggest files, you should now see full paths like 'packages/core/src/index.ts' rather than truncated versions. ai.title: Ctrl-C cancels agent response; run() returns sessionState on abort
ai.summary: Ctrl-C now aborts streaming agent responses in CLI, marking the last text block with '[response interrupted]' and resetting queue/streaming state. SDK run() no longer throws AbortError; it returns a RunState with sessionState preserved and output.type='error' on cancellation, enabling follow-up runs via previousRun. Changes touch cli/src/hooks/use-keyboard-handlers.ts, cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts, sdk/src/run.ts, plus README and examples.

eli5.text: If you're watching the assistant's reply stream live in the terminal and you hit Ctrl-C, the assistant will now stop mid-sentence and append a clear '[response interrupted]' note to the last chunk of text rather than silently cutting off, so you always know why the response ended where it did. When you build an app or script that calls the assistant (via the software development kit), cancelling a run no longer throws a hard error that crashes your program; instead it quietly returns a result object that still contains all the conversation history so far and marks the outcome as an error, letting your code decide what to do next. This makes it safe to write programs that let people cancel long-running replies and then continue the same conversation with a follow-up question.

ai.title: SDK version bumped to 0.9.0
ai.summary: The `@codebuff/sdk` package in `sdk/package.json` is now version `0.9.0`, up from `0.8.0`. This release bundles the recent SDK run() abort/cancellation handling changes, Ctrl-C interruption propagation, and the ErrorOr return-type refinements alongside CLI-side chat input, cursor, and status-line fixes.
ai.evidence: Modified `sdk/package.json` bumps the version field from `0.8.0` to `0.9.0` in the same-day commit sequence, releasing the prior changes described in the release updates.

eli5.text: This release makes the chat and command-line tool more reliable and pleasant to use, with better text display, smoother navigation through past commands, and a clearer double-key exit to prevent accidentally quitting. When you type long messages, the text now wraps correctly instead of breaking awkwardly, and when you scroll back through your previous inputs using the arrow keys, the cursor jumps to the end of the line so you can edit or resend without hunting for the right spot. Pressing Ctrl+C once now gives you a warning and a second press exits, so you won't lose work by mistake, and interrupting a running response cleanly marks it as stopped and keeps your session intact for continuing the conversation. The file-finding helper inside the tool is also smarter about listing every folder in a path, so it returns complete and accurate results instead of leaving out intermediate directories. Upgrading gives you a more stable, predictable experience where text behaves as expected, interruptions are handled gracefully, and navigation through your history stays smooth.

ai.title: Fix writetodos end-turn logic for multiple calls
ai.summary: The `hasOnlyFinishedTodos` check in `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` now evaluates all tool calls instead of strictly requiring a single call. This prevents premature turn termination when multiple `write_todos` calls are present but only some are completed. Logic updated to ensure turn ends only if every call is `write_todos` and at least one call contains fully completed todos.

eli5.text: When you ask an AI assistant to update its task list, it now keeps talking until every single todo on that list is marked done before the turn ends. Previously, if the assistant made several list updates at once, the system could mistakenly think the turn was over even when some items were still unfinished, causing the assistant to stop mid-plan. Now all the list updates must finish before the assistant wraps up and hands control back to you.

ai.title: CLI type safety refactor: remove as any, strict event typing
ai.summary: Refactored CLI type definitions and event handling to eliminate `as any` casts and improve type safety. `ContentBlock` union types in `cli/src/types/chat.ts` were split into named exports (`TextContentBlock`, `ToolContentBlock`, etc.), and `ToolName` usage was adjusted in `cli/src/components/tools/registry.ts` to satisfy strict typing via `satisfies`. In `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts`, `handleEvent` now uses type guards (`'agentId' in event`, `'totalCost' in event`) instead of unsafe property access, and subagent event matching was simplified to `subagent_start`/`subagent_finish` only, removing legacy hyphenated variants. A new `SetElement` utility type was added to `cli/src/types/utils.ts` to support strict tool name filtering in `isHiddenToolName`.

eli5.text: The CLI's behind-the-scenes type checking got stricter, so event handling now correctly distinguishes between different agent-related messages instead of treating them all the same. This affects developers building or modifying the CLI, reducing potential runtime errors from incorrect assumptions. You won't notice any visual or behavioral change when using the CLI, as it's a maintenance refactor that improves code reliability without altering functionality.

ai.title: use-send-message.ts replaces 'in' operator with has()
ai.summary: Switches from 'in' operator to has() helper for agentId and value checks in use-send-message.ts. Avoids potential runtime errors or type narrowing issues with the 'in' operator. Scope limited to cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts.

eli5.text: When the assistant logs the details of events it receives, it now uses a safer, more reliable check to decide whether a particular piece of data is present before it tries to read it. This reduces the chance of the logging step crashing when it encounters an unexpected event shape. You won't see any new features or visual changes; this is a small behind-the-scenes stability improvement to the event logging logic.

ai.title: Consolidate Ctrl-C message into StatusIndicator
ai.summary: Moved the 'Press Ctrl-C again to exit' message from `chat.tsx` into `StatusIndicator` in `status-indicator.tsx`. Updated `useHasStatus` hook to accept an object parameter including `nextCtrlCWillExit`. This centralizes status line rendering logic and simplifies `chat.tsx` by removing manual conditional text nodes.

eli5.text: The message that tells you 'Press Ctrl-C again to exit' now comes from the same part of the program that draws all the other status text at the bottom of the screen. That means the main window code no longer has to decide when to show that line itself. You won't see any difference in how or when it appears, pressing Ctrl-C once still prints the hint, and pressing it again still quits; the program just builds that text in a neater spot behind the scenes.

ai.title: Improve terminal tool component
ai.summary: Terminal tool component in `cli/src/components/tools/run-terminal-command.tsx` now displays command in bold next to bullet point, with output indented below. Output truncation limits display to 5 lines with mouse-clickable 'Show X more lines' toggle. Uses `useState` for expand/collapse state, `useTheme` for color styling, and `TextAttributes.BOLD` for command emphasis. Collapsed preview retains `$ ${command}` format.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to run a terminal command, the command now shows up in bold right next to the bullet point, with any output indented below it. If the output is longer than five lines, only the first five appear, and a clickable 'Show X more lines' link lets you expand the rest. Nothing else about the command experience changed; this just makes what the assistant ran and what came back a bit easier to read.

ai.title: OSC 10/11 terminal color detection
ai.summary: Added `terminal-color-detection.ts` to query terminal foreground/background colors via OSC escape sequences for theme detection. Updated `theme-system.ts` to prioritize OSC detection over platform defaults and added Zed terminal support. `login-modal.tsx` adjusted to use `theme.surface` instead of `theme.background`.

eli5.text: When you open CodeBuff in a terminal that reports its own colors (like certain terminal apps), it now picks the right light or dark theme automatically instead of guessing from the operating system. Your terminal is asked, 'Hey, what color is your background?' and CodeBuff matches that so text is easy to read. The login window also switches to a 'surface' color for its background instead of the main theme background, which keeps it looking consistent on more terminals. This works today in the CLI, for anyone whose terminal supports color-querying via OSC sequences.

ai.title: Fix CLI typecheck in StatusIndicator timer test
ai.summary: Updated `cli/src/components/__tests__/status-indicator.timer.test.tsx` to pass the required `nextCtrlCWillExit` prop to `StatusIndicator` and cleaned up unused imports. This resolves TypeScript compilation errors caused by a mismatch between the test mock and the component's current interface. Scope limited to CLI test suite.

eli5.text: The assistant's status display in the command line interface now correctly shows whether it is running or paused, without causing any hidden errors during testing. Developers fixed a small mismatch in how the display component is set up during tests, ensuring it receives the information it needs to work properly. If you were running the tool from a terminal, you would not see any difference in behavior today, but the team's internal checks will now pass cleanly.

ai.title: Add clientDisconnected and state to OpenRouter logger
ai.summary: Updates `web/src/llm-api/openrouter.ts` to include `clientDisconnected` and `state` in the warning logger payload during stream cancellation. This provides context for the 'Client cancelled stream' event. Internal logging change only.

eli5.text: The assistant quietly started recording extra details whenever someone stops an answer midway, like noting whether the connection had dropped and the current state of the session. This only affects internal logs that the team uses to debug issues, so you won't notice anything different in your conversations. If someone looked at those internal logs, they'd see this new information attached to the 'cancellation' entries, which helps explain why streams sometimes stay open after you stop them. It's already live today.

ai.title: CLI: disable slash menu during history navigation
ai.summary: Added mutual exclusion between slash command suggestions and input history navigation in the CLI. Implemented `lastEditDueToNav` state in `chat-store` to track programmatic updates from history arrows versus manual typing. `chat.tsx` uses this flag to toggle `suggestionMenuDisabled` and `historyNavEnabled`, preventing the menu from intercepting arrow keys or appearing when recalling commands. Refactored `setInputValue` across `router.ts`, `multiline-input.tsx`, and `use-chat-input.ts` to accept an `InputValue` object containing text, cursor position, and the navigation flag.

eli5.text: When you press the up and down arrow keys to scroll through your recently typed commands in the command-line assistant, the little menu of suggested slash commands (like /help or /settings) now stays hidden instead of popping up and grabbing those same arrow keys. This means recalling a previous command with the arrows won't accidentally open an overlapping menu or fight with it for control. It is live today in the command-line assistant, and you'll notice that using the arrow keys to browse your command history no longer triggers or interferes with the slash command suggestions.
